publish.description:
Same deck, same client - alag window. VedicHour aapke din ke saare 18 ghanton ko aapki apni birth chart ke against score karta hai, aur har ghante ke saath ek plain line deta hai - ki woh window kis kaam ke liye theek hai. Ek window clearer nikal sakta hai, doosra heavier. Sab kuch asli astronomical data se nikalta hai, andaaze se nahi, aur plain English mein likha jata hai. Decide phir bhi aap karte ho.

Apna free chart banao: https://www.vedichour.com/free-kundli?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=short&utm_campaign=launch_video&utm_content=same-pitch-v2
Sample din poora dekho: https://www.vedichour.com/sample-report

For reflection and planning only. Not medical, legal, financial, or emergency advice.

v2Notes: Selected as the highest-ranked banked decision-moment creative that could be made to pass pre-flight with a faithful edit. HOOK kept verbatim ('Same pitch. Do alag windows.') and so is the opening line ('Deck same hai. Client same hai.'). Three law fixes, no hook weakening: (1) every narrated shot removed - the whole script is now Veo native on-camera dialogue, so the reel has one voice and no synthetic narrator; (2) both product shots pointed away from the payment page to https://www.vedichour.com/sample-report, panning 4330->4820px so the 10-11 am 'Good for being seen - a pitch, a demo, or asking your boss for something' window and the 11-12 'pleasant but unfocused' window are both readable, and the pan deliberately starts below the 9-10 am card whose page copy uses off-brand best/worst wording; (3) the dilemma is stated as two windows rather than two weekdays so the proof on screen is exactly what the script claims - the sample report shows one real day's 18 windows.

linter.reason: Timing comparison with clearer/heavier framing, user decides, no promised outcome.
